meaning.evidence: Every joke and every claim survives, from "Vice Turkey" to "Yes, We Cran" and the "leftovers" close. Additions are colour hanging off the original: "longer than a wet week" on the campaign, "Not a gutless chook among 'em" after the chicken pun, "sticky fingers and all" on the children.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "on the bench" for the backup role, "let 'em off the hook" for clemency, "ankle biters" for children, "crook" for sick, "stinkers" for the bad jokes. "rustle him up a pair of aviator sunnies" is fine.

authenticity.evidence: Largely natural pub-yarn voice: "me great privilege", "this arvo", "every man and his dog has a feed". A couple of non-Aussie forms: "chuffed" is British, "folks" leans American.

register.evidence: A full level-5 yarn throughout, dropped g's and all ("pushin' on", "doin'-it-tough"). Swearing stays mild ("Too bloody right", "every poor bugger"), well within vulgarity 2.

tone.evidence: The jokes stay jokes and the serious middle stays warm and earnest: "We're a mob that looks out for each other and has each other's backs."

flow.evidence: Reads aloud easily; the long health-cover sentence with "millions of ankle biters among 'em, sticky fingers and all, who finally know they're covered if they get crook" runs a little long.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably Obama's last turkey pardon: the self-deprecating gags, the policy list, the inclusive creed, the pun-laden close.

problems.original: we're honored to be joined by two of the lucky ones

millions of ankle biters among 'em, sticky fingers and all
problems.why: "sticky fingers and all" is harmless colour but clutters an already long sentence.

A.summary: A full, natural level-5 retelling that keeps every joke and the earnest middle.

meaning.evidence: All points kept, including every pun ("cold turkey", "polls to poultry", "weren't chicken", "Yes, We Cran"). "Tot can't pull his weight on the day" shifts "can't fulfill his duties" slightly.

sense.evidence: Mostly exact ("on the mend", "let 'em off the hook this arvo", "a few shockers"). "pull his weight" means do a fair share, not be unable to perform, so it strains a little.

authenticity.evidence: Natural throughout: "That was a ripper, that one", "never been a walk in the park", "We're a mob that looks out for each other". "after a long arse of a campaign season" is a slightly awkward construction; "folks" leans American.

register.evidence: Clearly Aussie but nearer level 4 than 5: long stretches stay close to the original ("guided by values and ideals that have been a light to all of humanity"). Swearing ("bloody", "arse") is within vulgarity 2.

tone.evidence: Jokes land as jokes and the serious passages stay serious: "I reckon we're judged by how we look after the poor and the vulnerable".

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly; "a long arse of a campaign season" is the one clunky join.

variety.evidence: Reasonably varied ("stoked", "ripper", "sunnies", "arvo", "crook", "a feed", "shockers"); "reckon" recurs a few times.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the original speech, its jokes and its message intact.

problems.why: Awkward construction; "a bloody long campaign" would sit more naturally.

problems.why: "pull his weight" means do a fair share, not be unable to do the job.

problems.original: defined by values and ideals that have been a light to all humanity
problems.why: Several passages stay close to the original, light for level 5.

B.summary: Faithful and natural, a notch lighter than level 5.

meaning.evidence: Several lines change or garble the sense: "the brave turkeys who werea lucky bugger" inverts "weren't so lucky"; "we're cactus, stuffed on getting him a pair of aviator glasses" loses the meaning; "no matter what some drongo reckons" adds a jab not in the original.

sense.evidence: "cactus" (broken) and "stuffed" make no sense in "we're cactus, stuffed on getting him"; "proved that they weren't chook" breaks the chicken pun; "Yep, We Cran" breaks the "Yes, We Can" pun.

authenticity.evidence: Stage-Australian: stock interjections bolted onto sentence starts ("Crikey,", "Struth,", "Bugger me,", "Mate,"), plus US "Jeez Louise" and the original's "come one" typo left in.

register.evidence: Heavy slang and swearing reach level 5, but much text is the original untouched ("by an adherence to a common creed"), and the weight is uneven. "fuckin' oath" and "Oh, shit" are within vulgarity 2 but "every bastard" and "Faaaaaark me" push its spirit.

tone.evidence: "Oh, shit, and there are many families of servicemembers who had empty chairs at the table" makes the solemn passage flippant; "Faaaaaark me." ends the speech on a crude note it never had.

flow.evidence: Hard to read: "Struth, (laughter.)", "who werea lucky bugger", "the spirit of a hungry battlers", "values'n ideals".

variety.evidence: Leans on the same tics: "Anyway," three times, "bloody" repeatedly ("my bloody great privilege -- well, it's me bloody privilege").

essence.evidence: Recognisable as the turkey pardon, but the puns are broken and the earnest middle is undercut.

C.summary: Bolted-on slang and swearing, broken puns and garbled lines; the tone of the serious passages is undercut.
